observations:
Torah #241 is a short, eitza-dominant teaching of seven sentences. All concepts in the source text are accounted for within the two packages identified:

- Package 1 (מידת הדין, חמת ה', קנאה, דינים) — the divine judgment cluster
- Package 2 (צדיק גדול המשגיח בתיקון העולם, פינחס) — the tzaddik/Pinchas archetype

The remaining significant concepts examined for possible new-package status:

1. נְקָמָה (vengeance): Appears in 'לָבַשׁ נְקָמָה לִנְקֹם בָּהֶם' (line 4) and 'לָבַשׁ קִנְאָה לִנְקֹם בָּהֶם' (line 6) — clearly used interchangeably with קנאה. It could be added as a fifth node in Package 1. However, in this Torah it primarily describes the human act performed (the 'garment' Pinchas puts on), rather than the divine force itself. It does not form an independent domain — it is a near-synonym of קנאה and belongs in Package 1 if added.

2. רַחֲמִים (mercy): Appears only in line 7 as the conclusion — 'פינחס בוודאי היה רחמן ואחר-כך הֵקֵל הדינים מעליהם.' Mercy is the resolution and the antithesis of the judgment cluster; it is a single terminal node in an eitza flow (judgment is displaced → mercy follows), not a bechina cluster. One node does not form a package.

3. יִשְׂרָאֵל / בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל: Appear as the object of both the divine judgment and Pinchas's protection. They play a narrative/passive role and form no bechina family of their own in this Torah.

4. חִצַּי כָּלִים וְהֵם אֵינָם כָּלִים (the aggadic saying — 'My arrows are consumed but they are not consumed'): Cited as a proof-text supporting the principle that divine judgment cannot completely destroy. This is a quoted source, not a bechina-equivalent concept cluster.

Conclusion: No cluster of 3+ concepts connected by explicit bechina language forms an independent domain not already captured by Package 1 or Package 2. The teaching's architecture is fundamentally eitza (cause and effect), and the bechina content is limited to the three-name identification of the divine judgment force. No new package is warranted.
